description: RISK R-B, STATED FIRST BECAUSE THE CLASS NAME INVERTS THE BEHAVIOUR: the prompt-mandated class is TransactionViewController, but COTRN02C ADDS. app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:5 reads 'Function    : Add a new Transaction to TRANSACT file', and README.md:224 reads '| CT02 | COTRN02 | COTRN02C | Transaction Add     |' with the neighbouring README.md:223 giving CT01 and COTRN01C as 'Transaction View' - so the mapping is inverted against both the source header and the repository's own inventory. Rule R1 governs: the name is taken verbatim from the prompt and the behaviour from the source. Practice B4 requires the conflict be recorded here rather than silently repaired, so nothing is renamed, no case is downgraded to read-only, and the genuinely-viewing half stays parity/COTRN01C. PROVENANCE - STATICALLY DERIVED, NEVER CAPTURED (practice B12, risk R-A): every expected value below was derived by reading app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:193-230 and :576-604 against CVACT03Y's byte layout, app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY's input-item PICTURE clauses, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy's two 40-byte title literals and the real rows of app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt. Nothing here was captured from a live COBOL run, because execution is impossible in this environment: there is no z/OS, the available compiler's indexed-file handler is disabled, no Language Environment CEE service exists, there is no CICS emulator, and DFHAID and DFHBMSCA - which this program copies at :91-92 - are IBM-supplied and absent from the repository (risk R-D). That limit is stated where the expectation lives instead of being absorbed in silence. Because a derived expectation can encode a misreading where a captured one cannot, every line cited above is named so a reviewer can re-derive it. WHAT THIS CASE DRIVES: REENTER - CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT is 1 - with EIBAID DFHENTER, so RECEIVE-TRNADD-SCREEN runs and the ordered inline EVALUATE EIBAID at :133-152 takes its first arm into PROCESS-ENTER-KEY. VALIDATE-INPUT-KEY-FIELDS at :193 then takes arm 1 at :196, because ACTIDINI is neither spaces nor low-values. ACTIDINI is eleven digits, so the IS NOT NUMERIC guard at :197 does NOT fire - that guard firing is case08's subject, not this one - and :204-205 COMPUTE WS-ACCT-ID-N = FUNCTION NUMVAL(ACTIDINI) then :206-207 move the eleven-digit image into XREF-ACCT-ID and back over ACTIDINI, a PIC 9(11) source into a PIC X(11) receiver, which is why ACTIDINO returns eleven zero-padded digits. :208 performs READ-CXACAIX-FILE, whose EXEC CICS READ at :578-586 carries RIDFLD(XREF-ACCT-ID) KEYLENGTH(LENGTH OF XREF-ACCT-ID). The EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :588 has three arms and their order is itself behaviour, WHEN OTHER last (gate G30, rule R7): DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :589-590 is CONTINUE and is reached by the account-path cases that get past the lookup, of which case19's successful add is the clearest; DFHRESP(NOTFND) at :591-596 is THIS case; and WHEN OTHER at :597-603 belongs to case10, which forces that outcome and additionally emits the DISPLAY 'RESP:' WS-RESP-CD 'REAS:' WS-REAS-CD line at :598. This arm emits no DISPLAY at all, so no DISPLAY_LINE channel appears below. The mirror image on the card path is case11, which reaches READ-CCXREF-FILE's own NOTFND arm with 'Card Number NOT found...' and the cursor on the card field. THE ABSENT ACCOUNT ID WAS PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED (practice B1): all 50 rows of app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt were sliced at bytes 26 to 36, which is where CVACT03Y puts XREF-ACCT-ID PIC 9(11) after XREF-CARD-NUM X(16) and XREF-CUST-ID 9(09). Those 50 rows carry 50 distinct identifiers forming exactly 00000000001 through 00000000050, so 00000000099 is absent from every one of them. All 50 were scanned because the fixture is NOT in account-id order - it is ordered by XREF-CARD-NUM ascending, so row 0 holds the HIGHEST account, 00000000050 on card 0500024453765740, while account 00000000001 sits at row 48. A head-only scan would have been actively misleading. fixtures/cardxref.txt is byte-identical to that oracle, so the proof and the seed are the same data, and the oracle was read only (practice B3). CARDNIN IS ASSERTED UNCHANGED, AND THAT IS THE POINT (practice B5): SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN at :516-534 ends with EXEC CICS RETURN, so it is terminal and the task ends inside the rejection. :209 MOVE XREF-CARD-NUM TO CARDNINI is therefore never reached, VALIDATE-INPUT-DATA-FIELDS at :167 never runs, and the CONFIRMI EVALUATE at :169-188 never runs - hence no empty-field message and no confirm prompt. CARDNINI is seeded with 0500024453765740, a card number that IS present in the cross-reference at row 0 and resolves to account 00000000050. That is deliberate, so one value carries two assertions: CARDNINO must return those same sixteen digits rather than being overwritten from a record, and the read must have been issued on the ACCOUNT key even though the CARD key was perfectly resolvable, because EVALUATE TRUE takes its first matching arm. Had the two arms been reordered, this case would have resolved account 50 and succeeded instead of reporting NOT found. CONFIRMI is Y and the eleven data fields carry individually valid values for the same reason: expectedWrites being empty is then a positive assertion that not even an affirmative confirmation and a complete, valid transaction body can reach ADD-TRANSACTION past the short-circuit. The message keeps its upper-case NOT and its trailing ellipsis exactly as :592-593 spells them. NOT-FOUND IS A NORMAL OUTCOME, NOT AN EXCEPTION (gate G47): card.CardXrefRepository reports a discriminated result carrying a common.FileStatus outcome of NOT_FOUND together with the CICS RESP and RESP2, and it does not abend on the caller's behalf. COTRN02C contains ZERO CALL 'CEE3ABD', so there is no abend path to model here at all: expectedReturnCode stays 0, and gate G35 is not applicable and is deliberately not asserted. The controller turns the outcome into a screen message; treating not-found as a thrown error is the likeliest divergence and is ruled out explicitly. Gate G45 is honoured by the seeding: app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:63-65 defines FILE(CXACAIX) as DESCRIPTION(ALTERNATE INDEX TO CCXREF VIA ACCOUNT KEY) over the base cluster defined at :37-39, so this case seeds CCXREF ONCE and declares no separate CXACAIX input - the alternate index is an additional finder keyed on XREF-ACCT-ID over that one cluster, never a second table. The 36-byte rows are seeded RAW and are never pre-padded here: CVACT03Y sums to 50 as 16 + 9 + 11 + 14 (practice B11) while the data supplies only bytes 1 to 36, so the 14-byte FILLER shortfall is made up exactly once, at seed time, by the single validated normaliser that the CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 declaration below names (gate G16, risk R-F). Nothing pads again at comparison time, because a width disagreement is a difference rather than something to repair. ACCTDAT IS A DEAD DECLARATION AND IS SEEDED TO PROVE IT (practice B5): COTRN02C declares WS-ACCTDAT-FILE PIC X(08) VALUE 'ACCTDAT ' at :40 and copies CVACT01Y at :89, and names neither anywhere afterwards - the only DATASET operands in the whole program are WS-CXACAIX-FILE at :579, WS-CCXREF-FILE at :612 and WS-TRANSACT-FILE at :645, :676, :705 and :714. Fifty real 300-byte account records are seeded here and are still never read, which makes the deadness observable rather than merely asserted; no ACCTDAT entry appears in expectedWrites, in expectedFinalState or in expectedDatasets, and no normalisation is declared for it, because acctdata.txt is 300 bytes wide and CVACT01Y declares 300. Both declarations are preserved exactly as they stand - reading an account here would be a new feature and a parity violation. SHAPE AND EXPLICITNESS (practice B8): dataset binding KEYS only and never a dataset name, so no fully-qualified dataset name appears anywhere in this case (gate G46). The code page is named US-ASCII rather than defaulted, and the clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:34 so that POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :552-570 builds CURDATEO as MM/DD/YY and CURTIMEO as HH:MM:SS deterministically (practice B7). ERRMSGO is WS-MESSAGE moved from PIC X(80) into PIC X(78) at :520, so the 23-character message sits left-justified and space-padded and the two right-hand bytes of the 80-byte form are lost (rule R5); both widths are reported below as the two declared channels of ONE single message text, and there is no second, different message. The cursor is recorded as ACTIDINL: :595 positions it by moving -1 into that length item, a length item is validation metadata rather than payload, so it is reported under cursorField and never as a payload member - the payload names only input and output items, whose widths come from the symbolic map's PICTURE clauses. Conversation state travels entirely in the payload with no server-side session (rule R6, gate G37): the 218 bytes carried back are the 160-byte CARDDEMO-COMMAREA plus the 58-byte CDEMO-CT02-INFO of :72-80, which stays a separate DTO field rather than widening the context all seventeen controllers share. Commarea spans this case does not name take their picture's declared fill - spaces for PIC X, zeros for PIC 9. The unit is built as a plain object and its MAIN-PARA method is called directly, with no MockMvc, no HTTP and no JobLauncher in the path (gate G51). NO USER RULES EXIST: review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided', and that line is the whole document, so no user rule governs this file and none forced it into scope. The absence is stated rather than assumed and is NOT treated as licence to lower the bar: the standard held here is the Agent Action Plan's enterprise practices, cited above by name - B1, B3, B4, B5, B7, B8, B11 and B12 - together with rules R1, R5, R6 and R7. Gates G32 (this program contains zero GO TO), G35, G39 (no pagination) and G43 (no 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC) are not applicable and are deliberately not asserted.
